plan|en|4|1800|6|gas|.intro: Your home uses 106,000 gallons a year of water, and commuting adds 2,650 lbs of CO2 a year from the commute.

steps.text: Share the commute with one other person to save 1,320 lbs CO2 per year. You can connect through UTA Rideshare: carpool and vanpool.
Take the bus or TRAX to work 2 days a week to cut 1,060 lbs CO2 per year. Check UTA trip planner and passes to plan your ride.
Work from home 1 day a week, if your job allows, to save 530 lbs CO2 per year. Learn more through TravelWise, Utah Department of Transportation.

ask|en|4|1800|6|gas||does my lawn really.answer: Yards are the part of Utah's water use that households control most. In the Great Salt Lake basin, 26.8 percent of human-caused water depletions come from cities, homes and industry, while 91 percent of outdoor city water use is used up and does not flow back.

ask|en|4|1800|6|gas||which change should.answer: The top ranked action is to share the commute with one other person. It saves 1,320 lbs CO2 per year. The second action is to take the bus or TRAX to work 2 days a week, which saves 1,060 lbs CO2 per year.

ask|en|4|1800|6|gas||why is my air numbe.answer: Your commute adds up to 2,650 lbs of CO2 a year from driving 6 miles each way, which is about 3,000 miles a year. A typical gasoline car makes about 400 grams of CO2 a mile. Your total is still below the 9,300 lbs of CO2 from all driving one Utah resident typically does in a year.
